text: Queued ticket is the headless-extension spike (#1332), already worked twice with nothing to build. Checking what keeps re-queuing it before deciding.

I closed the headless-extension spike ticket (#1332), the only thing in the queue. Nothing needed building, so there's no branch or pull request. The queue is now empty.

**Why I closed it rather than working it again:** this was the third run on it. `triage quick` re-queues any ticket with Effort ≤ 2 and Uncertainty ≤ 2 every 6 hours. This one has Effort 1 and Uncertainty 2, so it kept coming back even though its own text says "do not queue before web runs come back." Both earlier runs found nothing to build and recommended closing, and so does its plan. The spike's question is answered: headless doesn't pass Cloudflare, but a minimized browser that isn't headless does, and that's what was built and merged. The only open item is Linux support, and nobody can use it until web runs return.

**Still open for you:**
- **GitHub issue #1332 is still open.** I only removed the ticket. The ticket said closing is your call, and the issue keeps the Linux note. If the issue changes, `update-tickets` will bring the ticket back. Close #1332 if you agree it's done.
- **The same loop can catch other tickets.** The triage rule has no way to tell a ticket that is waiting on something else from one that is ready. So any other ticket with Effort and Uncertainty of 2 or less that is waiting will be re-queued every 6 hours the same way.
